original.before: Law CI r5 item 4's P-1 to P-7 (unit CI-2; plan r3 LD-CIP-1, -2, -10, -11): charged native primitives for the component store, one native call each with no retry or fallback: the positioned chunk write, fchmod, the standalone F_FULLFSYNC barrier and its opaque handle-bound receipt, symlinkat and readlinkat, the no-follow close-on-exec kind-checked regular open and archive open, the no-follow entry status read and identity sample, and the one-flock pin released by close; P-7's status price equal to the filesystem's. Names, paths and targets are copied onto the stack, so no primitive allocates. macOS only; other targets refuse before any charge or call.
original.after: Law CI r5 item 4 P-1 to P-7 (CI-2; plan r3) and CI-A3 r4 (CI-3L): charged native component-store primitives, one call each with no retry or fallback: positioned write, fchmod, F_FULLFSYNC and handle-bound receipt, symlinkat/readlinkat, no-follow close-on-exec kind-checked regular/archive open, no-follow entry status/identity, and one-flock pin released by close. CI-3L adds absolute borrowed-CStr final-no-follow lstat and retained-directory fstat identity, each priced as a status read. Name/path/link-target copies allocate no heap storage; native-error/refusal carriers may allocate after refusal. This qualification discharges CI2-R2-NBO-1 as carried by CI2INV230-R1-NBO-1; no universal allocation-free claim. macOS only; unsupported targets refuse before charge or native call.

original.before: Law CI r5 unit CI-2 platform tests: each primitive's charge before its call and source-order guard, refusal before an unfunded call, P-7's identical expression, the barrier receipt bound to its exact handle, the one-flock pin with busy hand-back and close release, symlinks read never followed, and a counting global allocator in this test binary showing that no primitive allocates.
original.after: Law CI r5 CI-2 and CI-A3 r4 CI-3L platform controls: native primitives charge before calls, refuse unfunded work, preserve status-price equality, exact barrier receipt and pin lifetime, and never follow final symlinks. Launch-path lstat and retained-directory fstat verify kind/device/inode and charge order, with absent/non-directory/native-error partitions. Counting allocator controls cover name/path/link-target copying on measured routes only; error carriers may allocate after refusal, so these tests establish no universal allocation-free primitive or production/platform qualification.
